newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed after moderate session.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed after moderate session.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended mixed on Friday after a session marked by anti-government protests and profit taking in some recent strong sectors.
The TSE Composite 300 Index fell 9.08 points to close at 5549.78 in modest turnover of 72.7 million shares worth C$1.01 billion ($750 million).
Trade was thin, but effective as some players stayed home in anticipation of a labor protest which shut down the Toronto transit system.
Many traders stayed in the city overnight or arrived in the early morning to avoid transportation snarls.
Around midday, demonstrators pounded on the stock exchange's glass doors and tried to break into the building.
Riot police were moved into the vicinity of the stock exchange, but did not intervene. Rally organizers later moved the raucous group away from the doors of the exchange.
"It was a pretty normal day except that it got a little interesting around noon," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
In today's trading, Ketchen said investors took profits in conglomerates, consumer products and technology.
Gains in nine of 14 sub-groups were led by communications and pipelines.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 462 to 418 with 308 issues ending unchanged.
* Newbridge Networks Corp. extended Thursday's fall, dropping 3.10 to 38.70 on 1.5 million shares.
The company has said there are no corporate developments to account for the stock price fall, but analysts cited concerns about the company's second quarter results.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd. fell 0.65 to 33.20 after climbing in recent sessions due to strong earnings this week.
* Bema Gold Corp. sank 1.05 to 7.85 on 3.6 million shares after the mining company released disappointing drill results from its Chilean Cerro Casale project.
